meta.title: AACT graph assumption-test toolbox: slide tests mapped to LadybugDB schema
meta.scope: Raw Study/Sponsor/Facility/Intervention/Condition/MeshTerm properties and edges as loaded by ladybug_import.py, including HAS_MESH_CONDITION, HAS_MESH_INTERVENTION and IS_A. Excludes embed.py, all bert_embedding fields, preprocess.py encodings, and MAPS_TO_MESH_* similarity edges.
meta.working_question: See hypotheses. Before/after COVID uses covid_transition, covid_overlap_days, covid_disrupted, covid_period (features.py cut points 2020-03-01, 2022-01-01).
meta.subset: Any FILTERS selection. The ~300 US kidney cancer set was a sanity check; real runs use a much larger set, with a few chosen cases bootstrapped heavily.
meta.outcome: study_duration_days (start_date to completion_date); primary_duration_days as a secondary outcome

scopes.global: same condition filter, no country filter; needs a second select_study_ids() run, no code change

covid_fields._note: All before/after COVID tests use these Study fields from features.py; no new cutoffs are introduced.
covid_fields.covid_transition: start->completion category (pre_pre, pre_during, pre_post, during_during, during_post, post_post): main grouping for before/after contrasts
covid_fields.covid_overlap_days: days of the trial inside the COVID window: continuous exposure in the duration model
covid_fields.covid_disrupted: started before 2020-03-01 and completed on or after it: binary contrast
covid_fields.covid_period: start-based period: used only to split time series spans (start_date drives the series)

meta.why_graph: LadybugDB mirrors the AACT tables (from the pg_dump) as nodes and edges, so Cypher shows how the selected tables relate as they do in SQL, and derived features (covid_transition, covid_overlap_days, covid_disrupted) live on the Study node beside the source fields for a much larger set.
meta.goal: Examine links between average clinical trial duration and the COVID-19 pandemic.
aims: Predict average drug trial duration and estimate patient enrollment across disease areas.
Examine the relationship between trial duration and successful completion across the COVID-19 span in multiple therapeutic areas.
meta.population: All 545,294 AACT studies; drug trials = Study with HAS_INTERVENTION to Intervention.intervention_type = DRUG. US kidney cancer set was a sanity check.

missing_codes._note: features.py load_study_features() fills missing values before import, so LadybugDB has no nulls for these fields. Missingness tests must read raw ctgov.studies in Postgres, or treat these codes as missing.

derived_caveats.covid_overlap_days: Uses CURRENT_DATE when completion_date is null, so the value changes with the run date.
derived_caveats.followup_days: Computed as completion_date - primary_completion_date (post-primary follow-up), not schedule overrun as the SQL comment says.
derived_caveats.study_duration_days: Mixes Actual and Anticipated completion dates; split on completion_date_type.
derived_caveats.covid_stopped: Keyword match on why_stopped; 0 for every study without free text.

selection_filters.min_enrollment: enrollment > 0 drops studies whose enrollment was missing (coded 0) and real zero-enrollment withdrawals.
selection_filters.exclude_unknown_status: Drops UNKNOWN status, which AACT assigns to studies not updated in 2+ years; possibly related to disruption.

disease_area_*.kind: binary indicator per area (0/1), 25 columns from mesh.py DISEASE_AREA_MAP
disease_area_*.note: Multi-hot: a trial can be 1 in several areas. A trial with all zeros has no matched ancestor; treat it as "no area", not as missing at random.

MeshTerm.notes: Study links are leaf terms only (mesh_type = mesh-list). Ancestors reachable via IS_A edges, which are empty in lean mode (no NLM XML).

tests.assumption: COVID effect differs by therapeutic area and location
tests.method: For each area (value 1) x location (country globally; city in the US) cell with enough trials: COVID-vs-pre contrast in median duration, spread ratio (V1) and success rate, each with a bootstrap CI and permutation p-value. Correct across cells with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Show as a heat map of effect size (area rows x location columns) with non-significant cells greyed. A multi-area trial counts in each of its areas; a multi-site trial counts in each location (weights 1/k to keep totals honest). Confirm the pattern in V4 with (covid_transition | area) and (covid_transition | country) terms.
tests.pass_criterion: Cell flagged as a COVID hotspot if FDR-adjusted q < 0.05 and the CI excludes no change
tests.output: Area x location effect heat map + ranked hotspot table

clean.description: Drop studies with no HAS_MESH_CONDITION edge or no HAS_MESH_INTERVENTION edge; drop sentinel 0 / unknown values on fields used; ACTUAL completion dates only.
clean.risk: Intervention MeSH (browse_interventions) mostly covers drugs; procedure, radiation, behavioral and device trials often have none, so this filter is not random (test MS1).

designed_missing.description: Keep all studies; restore NaN where features.py coded 0/unknown (from raw ctgov.studies); then inject NaN and 0 deliberately under MCAR, MAR (missingness depends on phase or start year) and MNAR (long durations more likely missing) at 5, 10, 20 and 40 percent.
designed_missing.estimate: For each scenario and rate: bootstrap (B=2000) mean and median duration per MeSH group and per covid_period; record CI width, CI shift, and coverage of the clean-version estimate.

model.primary: V4 location-scale hierarchical model of log duration

access._note: Every test function takes an open LadybugDB connection and runs Cypher against the .kz database directly. Postgres is only needed where raw nulls matter (see needs_postgres).
access.db_path: LBUG_DIR=/database/database.kz (graph_data volume, mounted in jupyter and graph-pipeline)
access.connection: import real_ladybug as lb; db = lb.Database(LBUG_DIR, read_only=True); conn = lb.Connection(db)  # API assumed Kuzu-style; confirm read_only flag
access.single_writer: Open read-only. ladybug_import.py must not run at the same time; restart other notebook kernels that hold a lock.
access.id_filters: Never IN lists with special-character ids; use batched OR-chains (50-100 ids) with _esc(), as in fetch_embeddings().
access.scope_param: Each function takes study_ids (from select_study_ids) or None for the whole graph; US vs global is just a different study_ids list.
access.pattern: Pull each test frame once, cache as parquet keyed by (test id, FILTERS hash), then resample in numpy; never re-query inside a bootstrap loop.

heavy_bootstrap.note: For the few cases bootstrapped hard: vectorised numpy resampling in chunks of 10,000 to stay within memory; report percentile and BCa CIs and the Monte Carlo error of the CI ends.

hypotheses.claim: In 2020-2022 the distribution of time-to-completion tightened (lower spread around the mean).
hypotheses.note: Define cohorts by start date, never by completion date. Trials completing inside a 2-year window are capped in how long they can have run, which tightens spread by construction (V3 simulates this).

hypotheses.claim: The tightening is caused by COVID rather than other global factors.
hypotheses.note: Placebo windows, mix shift (phase, sponsor class, therapeutic area, intervention type), and known non-COVID breaks such as the FDAAA 801 Final Rule (effective 2017-01-18).
Bootstrap CIs on the SD/IQR ratio and posterior of the sigma contrast; correct for multiple therapeutic areas.

hypotheses.claim: Patterns differ by therapeutic area and patient population size.
hypotheses.note: Area-specific sigma and slope on log enrollment in the location-scale model.
